findings.problem: Grammar error in explain: after لم the verb must be jussive, so 'لم تكفي' should be 'لم تكف'.
findings.evidence: Arabic grammar (jussive after لم drops the final ya of a defective verb)

findings.problem: Text and scene disagree. The explanation says the driver of the broken-down car is approaching your lane and may enter the road suddenly. In the intro he walks to {dir:up, lane:1, shift:0.4}, so in the frozen question frame he is already standing inside lane 1 (your lane), not about to enter it.
findings.evidence: Scene intro: person 'to' {dir:'up', lane:1, y:49.6, shift:0.4}; me is in lane 1. Alternative fix (scene): walk him only to the lane edge (lane 'shoulder' with a negative shift, or lane 1 with shift of about 1.5) so the text stays as is

Near-duplicates, same concept 3 times: rd-010 (L5), pd-002 (L4) and hz-008 (L5) all show a vehicle stopped in the right lane before a zebra hiding a pedestrian. Their levels differ for the same idea.
Near-duplicates: jn-017 (L3) and hz-005 (L4) both show a long truck with its right indicator on, swinging left before turning right, with answer 'stay behind'.
Rain following gap: rd-017 and wx-004 both use 4 s (RTA), and wx-004 notes that Dubai Police press uses 5 s. These are consistent with each other, but check the q_ banks use the same figure.
Cyclist passing gap: pd-006, hz-007 and nt-001 teach 'at least 1 m', and the notes say S2 (Driving Safely in Dubai) gives 1.5 m. This must be settled the same way as the rules bank (HANDOFF stage 5).
unresolved: sb-002 (open question, verdict: the scenario is CORRECT). Executive Regulation (MR 130/1997) Art. 71 separates a 'single' road (both directions stop at least 5 m from the bus) from a 'dual' road (only traffic behind the bus stops). The RTA said, as reported in Gulf News on 2026-04-21 (S18 in the file), that divided roads are those separated by a median or a physical barrier, and undivided roads have no separation. Abu Dhabi Police and Emirates 24/7 (2026-08) describe the same thing: both directions stop on a two-way road without a physical barrier. A painted double solid line is not a median or a barrier, so under that definition drivers in both directions must stop. That is what sb-002 teaches. No source addresses a painted line on a 2+2 road explicitly, so this is an inference from the RTA definition, but a strong one. I could not open the regulation text (uaelegislation.gov.ae is blocked here), so the exact Arabic wording of Art. 71 (مفرد/مزدوج) was not checked. Sources: https://gulfnews.com/uae/transport/school-bus-stop-arm-rules-in-dubai-what-drivers-must-know-1.500514122 ; https://www.emirates247.com/uae-guide/uae-school-bus-stop-sign-rules-when-motorists-must-stop-and-the-fines-for-violations/4898 ; https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/08/31/uae-school-bus-rules-drivers-parents-students-staff/

pd-006 / hz-007 / nt-001: the minimum lateral gap when passing a cyclist (1 m vs 1.5 m). A web search found no UAE federal or RTA text that sets a number. The Dubai cycling resolutions (Exec Council 10/2015, 13/2022) cover riders, not passing distance. I left the items as they are.

jn-016 (opposing left turners pass in front of each other, 'to the left of the centre'): the geometry and answer agree with Art. 59 as summarised in research/rules.md F21 (turn just left of the centre). I could not reach the RTA handbook to confirm the exact wording. The item is already medium confidence and has a note.
